slides.title: Generator Data Pipelines
slides.prompt: Generators can be chained together to process massive streaming datasets in a memory-efficient pipeline. Each processing step pulls items lazily from the previous stage without loading full datasets into RAM.

slides.title: Chaining Pipeline Stages
slides.prompt: Fill in the variable name passed into filter_logs to establish the pipeline stream.

slides.title: Advantage of Generator Pipelines
slides.prompt: What is the key architecture benefit of building data pipelines using generators?
options: Data items are processed item-by-item through the pipeline, keeping RAM usage low regardless of file size
Pipelines run on separate GPU cores automatically
It guarantees transactional rollbacks for disk errors
slides.correctAnswer: Data items are processed item-by-item through the pipeline, keeping RAM usage low regardless of file size

slides.title: Consuming Pipeline Outputs
slides.prompt: Fill in the built-in accumulator function used to sum outputs streaming through a pipeline.

slides.title: Handling Large Files via Generator Pipelines
slides.prompt: Which file opening practice combined with generators ensures low memory usage for multi-gigabyte log analysis?
options: Iterating directly over the open file object line-by-line using a generator
Loading lines into a dictionary before yielding
Reading the whole file into bytearray
slides.correctAnswer: Iterating directly over the open file object line-by-line using a generator

slides.title: Lazy Mapping Pipeline
slides.prompt: Fill in the built-in function that lazily maps transformations across a generator stream.

slides.title: Pipeline Execution Evaluation Mode
slides.prompt: When does calculation actually take place in a multi-stage generator pipeline?
options: Only when an end terminal action (like a for-loop, sum(), or list()) requests items
Immediately as each pipeline stage function is instantiated
When the Python script finishes execution during exit
slides.correctAnswer: Only when an end terminal action (like a for-loop, sum(), or list()) requests items
